shows.title: Tide of Returns
shows.artist: Repatriates Collective (Verena Melgarejo Weinandt, Khadija von Zinnenburg Carroll, and collaborators)
shows.description:
Tide of Returns takes on one of the thorniest live issues in museum politics — the repatriation of looted and displaced cultural objects — and stages it as an immersive, sensory installation rather than an argument. The centerpiece, From My Mother's Country, floods the nave of the former Church of San Lorenzo with sand carried in part from the Gulf of Carpentaria in Australia and thousands of shell-and-fabric figures modeled on Dadikwakwa-kwa, sacred dolls recently returned to the Warnindilyakwa people by Manchester Museum. Video and sound documenting the objects' remaking and their journey back to community hands run through the installation, turning restitution into something felt in the body rather than just read about.

Alongside it, Verena Melgarejo Weinandt's Weaving Connections uses three-channel video of braiding, washing, and preparing textiles to think through how German cultural institutions have historically fabricated and displayed Indigenous identity — and what it costs to unwind that. Blue-toned threads and black braids recur through the piece as a visual rhyme for water's own capacity to connect and cleanse.

Curated by Khadija von Zinnenburg Carroll as part of her long-running Repatriates research project, the exhibition draws on real, recent cases — Namibia's restitution from Berlin, Australia's from Manchester — without illustrating them literally. It's a fitting subject for Ocean Space, whose whole program treats water as a connective and reparative force, and one of the more quietly urgent shows to see during this Biennale year.

shows.title: Sharing Legacy
shows.description:
Sharing Legacy pairs the late feminist sculptor Nancy Azara with her longtime partner Darla Bjork, a painter and practicing psychiatrist, in a show built around forty years of shared life rather than shared style. Azara's carved and gilded wood sculptures, drawn from matriarchal archetypes and the recurring image of the tree as body and ancestor, sit alongside Bjork's encaustic paintings and drawings, which mine the layered, half-hidden textures of the psyche. Both artists trained through the New York Feminist Art Institute, and that grounding shows in the show's insistence on gesture and material as forms of testimony.

What holds the two practices together is less subject matter than temperament: an expressionist handling of surface, a comfort with roughness and accretion, and an interest in what sits beneath the visible layer of a work. Seeing Azara's totemic, weathered forms next to Bjork's warm, waxy fields makes a quiet case for collaboration as a kind of portraiture — two people's decades together rendered obliquely through their separate tools.

Curated by Jen Dragon and Fanny Perez, the exhibition is a fitting late tribute to Azara, whose sculpture helped define a generation of feminist art practice in New York, and a chance to see her work in dialogue rather than isolation.

shows.title: Future Light
shows.description:
Future Light brings Gabriella Kirby back to the Veneto village her grandparents left after the Second World War, and the homecoming gives the show its emotional charge. Working across canvas, paper, and plaster, Kirby builds mixed-media compositions that move between plant, animal, and human form, looking for the protective and communicative structures — skins, membranes, roots — that let fragile things survive.

The paintings favor organic, gestural abstraction over illustration: trembling edges, layered plaster, and forms that read as both wound and shelter. Vulnerability and memory are the explicit themes, but the more interesting undercurrent is inheritance — how trauma and resilience travel across generations and continents, surfacing here in materials that themselves feel weathered and built-up over time.

Arriving in Venice during the 61st Biennale, two generations and seventy-five years after her family's emigration, Kirby treats the return less as nostalgia than as a way of testing what persists. It's a small, personal show, but one whose questions about belonging and renewal reach well past the artist's own family history.

shows.title: Yields of Fray
shows.description:
Leo Frontini's *Yields of Fray* is the Los Angeles-based painter's first European solo exhibition, timed to the 61st Venice Biennale and organized by the curatorial platform Private Waters with the Boateng Family Art Foundation. The show gathers eight paintings, two works on paper, and three marble sculptures made in 2025 and 2026, all pulled from a single body of work in which the artist stages scenes suspended between waking life and invented, parallel realities.

Frontini treats canvas, paper, and stone as three dialects of the same language: recurring figures migrate between a painted vision, a pencil study, and a carved form, so that a single dreamlike image can be read across media within the same room. The work draws on memory and the subconscious, letting tender and unsettling registers sit side by side — a strategy closer to symbolist narrative painting than to straightforward figuration, with the marble pieces grounding the more hallucinatory paintings in physical weight.

It's a compact but ambitious show for an artist still early in his career, arriving in Venice on the strength of two well-received gallery exhibitions in New York and Los Angeles. Seeing the sculptures and paintings together, in the intimate rooms of SPARC* just off Campo Santo Stefano, gives a clearer sense of how Frontini's imagery moves between mediums than any single-medium presentation could.

shows.title: Peggy Guggenheim in London: The Making of a Collector
shows.description:
Before there was a palazzo on the Grand Canal, there was a single room in Mayfair. This exhibition, the first large-scale museum show devoted to it, reconstructs Guggenheim Jeune, the gallery Peggy Guggenheim ran in London for eighteen months between January 1938 and June 1939, and argues that everything she later became as a collector was worked out there first.

The gallery's brief, restless program gets rebuilt here through roughly a hundred works and a trove of archival material: Kandinsky's first solo show in London, a Cocteau exhibition, an early UK collage survey, and a sculpture show that scandalized the press. Paintings by Kandinsky, Mondrian, Sophie Taeuber-Arp, Wolfgang Paalen, Rita Kernn-Larsen, Barbara Hepworth, and Henry Moore stand in for what actually hung on those walls, alongside photographs, letters, and gallery ephemera documenting the friendships, with Marcel Duchamp among them, that steered Guggenheim's eye toward abstraction and Surrealism.

It's a smart, research-driven complement to the permanent collection one floor away: instead of just marveling at the finished Venice museum, you get to watch its taste get formed in real time, through gambles and failures as much as triumphs. The show travels next to the Royal Academy and the Guggenheim in New York, but seeing it in the city where Peggy eventually settled, a short walk from the works she went on to buy, gives it a particular charge.

shows.title: Aghrab Idrāk: Thresholds of Perception
shows.artist: VCUarts Qatar research labs (31 artists and researchers)
shows.description:
Ten research labs from the Qatar branch of Virginia Commonwealth University's art school fill the rooms of a Zattere palazzo with light, sound and material experiments about how people perceive the world. There is a sound and light piece on Qatar's journeys between desert and sea, a work joining South Asian bandhani textiles with Arabic lettering, a film installation about women's memories of home and loss, and a kinetic sculpture that cleans the air.

A sound lounge turns the majlis into a field-recording space, a one-eyed AI robot watches visitors, and video portraits celebrate Qatar's gamer and geek communities. Rather than a single story, the show is a set of linked encounters shaped by the Gulf's histories of travel and exchange.

venue.name: Aghrab Idrāk: Thresholds of Perception
venue.address: Palazzo Cavanis, Dorsoduro 920, Fondamenta Zattere ai Gesuati

shows.title: Scotland + Venice: Bugarin + Castle (Shame Parade)
shows.description:
Davide Bugarin and Angel Cohn Castle, working as Bugarin + Castle, bring Scotland's presentation to a garden courtyard on Venice's Castello shore. Under the title Shame Parade, the duo revive rough music and charivari, the old European street rituals in which neighbours banged pots and paraded offenders to shame them, and set them beside Filipino and Scottish histories of public punishment.

The work mixes jewelled, costumed figures, a loud sculptural kiosk and a moving-image piece with a sound system, in a queer and trans reading of who gets shamed and who gets to make the noise. It was curated by Mount Stuart Trust and travels to the Isle of Bute in 2027.

shows.title: Catalonia in Venice: Claudia Pagès Rabal, Paper Tears
shows.description:
Paper Tears is an immersive installation in a former shipyard that treats paper watermarks as small political signs. Pagès Rabal works from an archive of fifteenth-century watermarks from Catalan paper mills, redrawing them as hand-made animations.

LEDs, lasers, drones and sound turn those marks into moving light and figures across the brick hall, so the faint signatures that once identified makers and trade routes become something to walk through.

The project follows how infrastructures of power leave traces in everyday materials, a theme the artist has pursued as a performer and writer as well as a visual artist.

shows.title: Iván Tovar: Le Retour
shows.dates_note: Biennale's page gives 29 Sep to 17 Nov; the organiser's page says 9 May to 22 Nov
shows.description:
Le Retour brings paintings and sculptures by the late Dominican artist Iván Tovar back to Venice, where he showed at the 1972 Biennale. Made between the 1960s and the 2010s, the works are glossy, dream-coloured scenes of knotted, bone-white and flesh-toned figures on dark or pastel grounds, in the line of European Surrealism but with a Caribbean palette and inventiveness.

The show treats Tovar as a case for Surrealism as a truly international movement rather than a European import. Small sculptures sit in bright display cases beside framed canvases, and rooms painted teal, navy and lavender set off each group of works.

venue.name: Iván Tovar: Le Retour
venue.address: Ex Istituto Idrografico, Museo Storico Navale, Riva San Biasio, Castello 2148

shows.title: Jacone’s Polyphony Exhibition from Macao, China
shows.artist: Eric Fok Hoi Seng, O Chi Wai, Veronica Lei Fong Ieng
shows.description:
Macao's presentation follows Wu Li, the seventeenth-century Chinese painter and poet who converted to Catholicism, took the name Jacone and never reached the Europe he set out for. Three Macao artists answer his story in installations that mix history, model-making and video.

Outdoor timber structures and a telescope piece linking old Macao with Rome lead into the Arsenale rooms, where cardboard screens carry moving images and a salt-crystal model of a Macao building sits on a plinth. The show is about migration, faith and the traffic between East and West, in tune with this year's Biennale theme of minor keys.

shows.title: Baile, Botella y Baraja
shows.description:
A multimedia installation of images and sound around the late Puerto Rican painter José Ruiz (1936-2015). The title comes from the nineteenth-century colonial formula of dance, bottle and cards used as social control, which Ruiz's naive-style paintings turn into counter-memory.

The soundscape runs from bomba to perreo. Curator is REM Escobar; Monica Parada is listed as an exhibitor.

shows.title: Kan Yasuda: Isole del Silenzio
shows.description:
Kan Yasuda fills a dim, white-floored hall with ten smooth marble forms, oval and round, set out like islands in a mineral garden. Raking light from the walls lets each stone seem to float, and the shapes read differently as you move around them. Some are hollowed, so empty space becomes part of the sculpture.

The show is built around quiet and slowness: fullness against emptiness, weight against lightness. A video, Beyond Form, shows how the marble is worked, and visitors are invited to feel the cool, polished surfaces.

venue.name: Kan Yasuda: Isole del Silenzio
venue.address: Corte Nuova, Fondamenta de l’Abazia, Cannaregio 3560

shows.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
shows.description:
Fermata presents five installations by Kingsley Ng and Angel Hui that find Hong Kong in everyday Venetian moments. Ng's Laundry Nocturne projects light and sound onto laundry strung between buildings, and Hui's I Would Like to Open a Window for You is a wrought-iron window frame made with local Hong Kong metalsmiths.

The pause of the title is meant literally: small stops in daily life. The Hong Kong Museum of Art organises it, taking over from M+ this year.

shows.title: Fondazione Bvlgari presents in Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana
shows.description:
Fondazione Bvlgari's first exhibition pairs two artists in the Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana. Lara Favaretto closes her Momentary Monument series with The Library, turning the Sansovino reading room into a library inside a library, built from thousands of salvaged books.

Monia Ben Hamouda's Fragments of Fire Worship places two neon sculptures in the vestibule, so visitors pass through them on the way in. She is the 2025 MAXXI Bvlgari Prize winner.

The pairing sets an artist known for impermanent monuments beside a younger one working in light and ritual symbols.

venue.name: Fondazione Bvlgari at the Biblioteca Marciana
venue.address: Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana, Piazzetta San Marco 13/a

shows.title: Hybrids. Leandro Erlich al Negozio Olivetti
shows.description:
Leandro Erlich, best known for illusionistic architecture, shows a body of about twenty sculptures that fuse animal, plant and human forms. A snail with a human hand, a bronze serpent clasping hands, a crystal cluster and a rose-like form with a model house inside it sit among Carlo Scarpa's showroom fittings.

The works are in marble, bronze, ceramic and glass, and many are new. The idea of the hybrid, a creature that is no longer one thing, is presented as the ordinary condition of people today rather than an exception.

The setting matters: Scarpa's 1958 Olivetti shop in Piazza San Marco, run by the FAI, gives the sculptures a modernist stage of stone, glass and polished floors.

shows.title: Lee Ufan
shows.description:
A survey in the eight rooms of SMAC, curated by Dia's Jessica Morgan, follows Lee Ufan's painting across seven decades, from the Korean and Japanese movements he helped shape to the calm, nearly empty canvases of his later series. Large cream and white canvases carry a single brushed bar or a few blocks of fading blue and red pigment, and a wall of dense dots marks his earlier work.

Three installations pair stones with steel plates, glass and gravel, and a thicket of dark reeds rising from sand, two of them made for Venice. The show is a timed reflection on space, matter and the gesture of the hand, shown in the artist's ninetieth year.

venue.name: Lee Ufan at SMAC
venue.address: SMAC – San Marco Art Centre, Piazza San Marco 105

shows.title: Screen Melancholy: Li Yi-Fan
shows.description:
Li Yi-Fan's Taiwan pavilion fills the old prison rooms of Palazzo delle Prigioni with pale, 3D-printed bodies and fragments, among them giant hands and feet scattered across the stone floor, and with screens playing his computer-made films. The hairless, puppet-like avatars of his videos wander through cluttered studios, theatres and glitching green-screen worlds, haunted by eyes, masks and automated voices.

Curated by Raphael Fonseca and organised by Taipei Fine Arts Museum, the show is about the strain of living inside images, from generative AI to endless feeds, and the nervousness of a place whose status is always in question. Some of the sculptures double as seats with phone chargers, tying bodily fatigue to screen dependence.

shows.title: Cymru yn Fenis / Wales in Venice presents Sownd: Manon Awst and Dylan Huw
shows.description:
Sownd is an immersive sculptural environment by Manon Awst and Dylan Huw, built from organic materials, found objects and text, sound and architectural elements. It grows from the artists' research into Welsh peatlands, sticky unstable ground that hides and exposes deep material history.

The show is curated by Steffan Jones-Hughes, led by Oriel Davies and Oriel Myrddin, and extends into events on peat sites across Wales through the summer.

venue.name: Wales in Venice
venue.address: Istituto Santa Maria della Pietà, Castello 3703, Calle della Pietà

shows.title: Infinito Cabinet. Maria Cristina Crespo
shows.description:
Infinito Cabinet is a contemporary Wunderkammer that sits between Malraux's imaginary museum and Borges's cosmic library. Crespo gathers anthropomorphic vessels, stage-like settings, painted backdrops and costumes, often from recycled fabric, into a journey through literature, myth, religion and philosophy.

It draws on Dante, Pasolini and Mithras and on places from the Mediterranean to Mexico and Asian deserts, and answers cancel culture by treating Western identity as a resource. Curator is Giusy Caroppo.

shows.title: Nalini Malani: Of Woman Born
shows.description:
Nalini Malani fills a long brick warehouse on the Zattere with a nine-channel animation work drawn on iPads, projected onto the walls in red, orange and white line. Faces of screaming, weeping and watching women appear and dissolve, with handwritten words such as 'I am tired' and 'unbearable' stitched across the surfaces, and thin lines connect the figures like a web.

The work builds on her Animation Chambers series and takes the myth of Orestes and the killing of a mother as its core, setting violence, motherhood and the fate of women against the present. It was commissioned by the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art and curated by Roobina Karode.

venue.name: Nalini Malani: Of Woman Born
venue.address: Magazzini del Sale n. 5, Dorsoduro 262, Fondamenta Zattere ai Saloni

shows.title: Ricamatrici palestinesi (The Gaza Genocide Tapestry)
shows.description:
The Gaza Genocide Tapestry is a hundred-panel cross-stitched record of the destruction of Gaza since October 2023, made by Palestinian women in the occupied West Bank, in refugee camps in Lebanon and in the diaspora as far as New Zealand. Each panel uses tatreez, the traditional embroidery that carries village and family identity, to mark a lost neighbourhood, landmark or household.

It is the latest chapter of the Palestine History Tapestry, which follows the land's story from the Neolithic to today. The presentation treats slow collective stitching as testimony: a record that cannot be scrolled past.

shows.title: Ronald Ventura: Luna
shows.description:
Luna is a new body of work by the Filipino artist Ronald Ventura that ties Venice to Malabon, the fishing town near Manila, through water and the moon's pull. Giant charcoal-grey drawings of drifting figures and heaps of debris hang beside resin and Murano glass sculptures, among them a plumbing-pipe saint, a winged figure on a column, a monumental head lying on its side and a crab holding a glass bowl.

The pieces speak of waste, salvage and weathered monuments, and of communities who live with rising water. The show sits in a former shipyard in Castello and picks up the Biennale's theme of minor keys through its quiet, nocturnal tone.

shows.title: Song E Yoon: Songs Across Time
shows.artist: Song E Yoon, Frédéric Bruly Bouabré
shows.description:
Song E Yoon, a Korean artist based in New York, is shown with the late Ivorian draughtsman Frédéric Bruly Bouabré in a pairing about writing before language. Yoon's large canvases and drawings borrow from rock engravings, myth and star maps, with spattered acrylic in acid yellow, red and violet and a deer drawn on a glowing ground, while a floor of dark fur gives one room the feel of a cave.

Bouabré's small coloured-pencil cards, each framed with a border and numbered, set out the alphabet he devised for the Bété language and pictures of everyday things. The curator Seohyun Kang reads Bouabré's pieces as a language of record and Yoon's as a language of journey.

venue.name: Song E Yoon: Songs Across Time

shows.title: Su Xiaobai's Alchemical Universe
shows.description:
Twenty-three lacquer paintings by Su Xiaobai, made between 2009 and now, plus his first lacquer piece from 2003, are hung in the frescoed rooms of a Cannaregio palazzo. Thick, domed slabs in jade green, turquoise, ash white and smoky black carry scratched, abraded and crazed surfaces that look like weathered stone or the sky behind cloud.

Twelve works come from his newest Niao Niao series, quiet monochromes named for fleeting things such as moonlight on snow or a far bell, which suit the Biennale's minor-key theme. The exhibition was curated by Stephen Little of LACMA and designed by WHY Architecture.

venue.name: Su Xiaobai at Palazzo Soranzo Van Axel

shows.title: Tadeusz Kantor (1915-1990): Emballage, Cricotage and Madame Jarema
shows.description:
The show sets out more than sixty works by the Polish artist and theatre maker Tadeusz Kantor, from dark, gouged informel paintings of the late 1950s and his wrapped-object emballages to the last painting series, with film of his stage piece The Dead Class and pieces from the theatre itself such as mannequins and a school bench.

Beside him is Maria Jarema, his colleague in founding the Cricot groups, represented by bright overlapping-shape monotypes and by costumes she made for Kantor's first productions in the 1950s. Together they show how painting, performance and objects fed each other in Polish postwar avant-garde.

shows.title: Vyacheslav Akhunov: Instruments of the Mind
shows.description:
Vyacheslav Akhunov, a founding figure of conceptual art in Central Asia, is shown in his first Venice survey, covering five decades of painting, drawing, video and installation. Layered handwritten text covering Soviet magazine pictures of athletes and schoolgirls, ink drawings of hands, heads and winged forms, and a collage of stone heads all treat repetition as a way of thinking, like a mantra that wears words down to sound.

Several works were conceived in the 1970s as sketches and are built for the first time here. The show, curated by Sara Raza for CCA Tashkent, looks at how the Soviet picture world can be turned against itself, and at memory, spiritual reflection and the passage of time.

shows.title: Constellations: Group exhibition in support of Picha Art Center
shows.artist: Jermay Michael Gabriel, Justin Randolph Thompson, Lamar Robillard, Délio Jasse, Ako Atikossie, Désiré Lumuna, Beya Gille Gacha, Jean Katambayi Mukendi
shows.description:
Constellations is a benefit group show for PICHA Art Center in Lubumbashi, an independent contemporary art centre in the Democratic Republic of Congo that runs exhibitions, residencies and education programmes and organises the Lubumbashi Biennale. Money from the sale of the works goes to the centre's programmes.

Eight artists from Africa and its diaspora take part. Délio Jasse prints old archive photographs on cloth and stamps them in red; Ako Atikossie and Jermay Michael Gabriel show dense graphic works on paper; Jean Katambayi Mukendi sews a looping, thread-covered form on a dark ground; Désiré Lumuna draws explanatory diagrams and a pregnant silhouette; Lamar Robillard hangs a black fabric piece; Justin Randolph Thompson shows a wooden rack and small dark forms on the wall; and Beya Gille Gacha contributes a portrait with a blue-painted face.

The show was organised with Black History Month Milano and Black History Month Firenze and treats the group as a constellation of separate voices.

venue.name: AKKA Project Venice
venue.address: Ca’ del Duca 3052, Corte del Duca Sforza, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Albedo: You see me in the twilight
shows.description:
Giovanni Ozzola built Albedo for the two old fourteenth-century warehouses that face each other across a canal beside Campo San Polo. A short boat crossing joins the two spaces, so the canal becomes part of the route.

The show opens with a hanging cluster of ship's bells, Dust on my memories, held silent. A video installation, Matteo, rises from one of the water gates on an LED wall: a blind archer at the moment of release, a moving statue whose gesture never repeats. Beyond the crossing, a dark hall gathers photographs of Venice at night, among them a lighthouse in the dark, lit by the water-gate daylight.

Sound and light work as tools for finding a position in space and time, and the exhibition reads as a journey through thresholds and signals. It was made with Galleria Continua for the 61st Biennale.

venue.name: Beatrice Burati Anderson Art Space & Gallery
venue.address: Beatrice Burati Anderson, Calle de la Madonna, 1976, 30125 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Off the Map
shows.description:
Roselena Ramistella's Off the Map follows teenagers and families on three small Italian islands, Pantelleria, Linosa and Capri, in the months after the summer visitors leave. About a hundred photographs move between portrait, landscape and documentary: two faces side by side, a lit headland, a swimmer bent over wet rock, a ferry-side view of a harbour town, a dark sea.

The project was commissioned by Sanlorenzo and the Sanlorenzo Foundation, which works with island communities on education, health and inclusion, and it appeared first in the yacht builder's yearly almanac with texts by Chiara Barzini. Ramistella, a Sicilian photographer who has worked on rural and fishing communities for years, treats the islands as conditions of life and asks what growing up at a distance does to a person's sense of the future.

It is the closing event of Casa Sanlorenzo's 2026 programme, curated by Cristiano Seganfreddo.

shows.title: Joe Diggs: In Venice
shows.description:
Joe Diggs, long known for figurative paintings of his family and the African-American community on Cape Cod, shows a new turn toward abstraction at Castello 925. His pictures here layer overlapping circles, patterns and colour fields that read as a memory of traditional woven surfaces.

The show answers the Biennale's title, In Minor Keys, by giving attention to quiet, spiritual and personal registers rather than grand statements. It was curated with Castello 925's Jen Dragon and Luca Caldironi and runs alongside Whitney Hagen's show at the gallery's annex.

Diggs is represented by Berta Walker Gallery and was named Artist of the Year by the Arts Foundation of Cape Cod in 2025.

venue.name: Castello 925
venue.address: Fondamenta S. Giuseppe, 925, 30122 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Chromatic Conditions
shows.description:
Whitney Hagen shows new paintings at the Castello 780 annex under the title Chromatic Conditions. Her abstract canvases work with vivid colour, shifting flat planes and architectural shapes to suggest a hidden geometry of space and time.

Like the neighbouring Joe Diggs show, it takes its cue from the Biennale's theme, In Minor Keys, and asks for slow looking at how colour and edge change what a space feels like.

The exhibition was organised by Castello 925, whose annex at Fondamenta San Giuseppe 780 hosts it.

venue.name: Castello 925
venue.address: Fondamenta S. Giuseppe, 925, 30122 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Richard Marquis and his Murrine, featuring Mathieu Grodet and Denise Barr
shows.artist: Richard Marquis, Mathieu Grodet, Denise Barr
shows.description:
Richard Marquis, the American glassmaker who learned the murrine technique at the Venini furnace on Murano in 1969, is shown here as an artist of the murrine itself: the small slices cut from fused glass canes, each one a tiny picture. His playful vessels and objects, made at his Puget Sound studio, show how far he has pushed a technique that is more than a thousand years old.

French-born glassmaker Mathieu Grodet answers with his own murrine, so the two approaches to the same demanding craft sit next to each other, one an American pioneer of studio glass and the other a younger maker working in Canada.

Denise Barr adds jewellery set with murrine she received from Marquis, mounting them with silver, toy cars and found objects. The show was organised with R & Company of New York and sits in the gallery's Venice space during the Murano glass season.

shows.title: 25 Years of La Galleria: Art Beyond Boundaries
shows.artist: Rashid Al Khalifa, Lore Bert, Hellmut Bruch, Daniel Buren, Eduardo Chillida, Sebastian Dannenberg, Heinz Gappmayr, Hans-Jörg Glattfelder, Nigel Hall, José Heerkens, Gottfried Honegger, Mohammed Kazem, Wulf Kirschner, Joseph Kosuth, Carolin Liebl und Nikolas Schmid-Pfähler, Christian Megert, François Morellet, Nam Tchun-Mo, Fabrizio Plessi, Arne Quinze, Mario Reis, Vera Röhm, Turi Simeti, Günther Uecker, Guang Yao Wu
shows.description:
To mark twenty-five years of La Galleria, the Venice branch of Dorothea van der Koelen's Mainz gallery, this anniversary show gathers works by about thirty artists from fourteen countries who have been part of its story. It is a themed exhibition on the idea of art beyond boundaries, and it is a gallery programme running beside the Biennale rather than an official collateral event.

The core of the show is constructive and conceptual art. There are Francois Morellet's neon and line pictures, Turi Simeti's embossed ovals, Gunther Uecker's nail reliefs, Heinz Gappmayr's word pictures, Hans-Jorg Glattfelder's pyramid relief, Daniel Buren's striped frames and Joseph Kosuth's clock. Around them sit Lore Bert's paper objects, Mohammed Kazem's waves, Rashid Al Khalifa's perforated circles and Nam Tchun-Mo's red and blue relief pieces.

Later and more playful pieces include Arne Quinze's twisting colour sculpture, Fabrizio Plessi's video wall and Carolin Liebl and Nikolas Schmid-Pfahler's glass flowers.

venue.name: Galerie Dorothea van der Koelen
venue.address: Calle Calegheri, Fondamenta Narisi, 2566, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: The Materiality of Judy Chicago
shows.description:
Judy Chicago's solo show in Venice follows her career through the materials she has used rather than through dates. Spray-painted car hoods, porcelain painted with china paint, needlework, drawing, glass and bronze sit side by side, each treated as a serious medium at a time when several of them were dismissed as craft.

The old and the new meet in the same rooms: a test plate from The Dinner Party, an early drawing of rings from 1968, a recent hood and a prismacolor study of lilies, then a newly made series of glass and bronze sculptures, Lilies/Goddesses, that make their first appearance here. The series grew out of a 2024 lily installation made for Arles and was produced with the Murano glassworks of Studio Berengo.

Curator Allison Raddock arranged the show as a tour of Chicago's most important series, ending with her latest pieces, and a catalogue with an interview by Massimiliano Gioni accompanies it.

venue.name: Galleria Alberta Pane
venue.address: Calle dei Guardiani, 2403 H, 30100 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Projects and Installations, Venice
shows.description:
This tribute to Fabrizio Plessi, the Venetian pioneer of video sculpture who died on 23 August 2026, shows the projects and installations behind his work with water, fire and screens. The gallery has gathered large drawings in which he planned his installations, annotating them in ink and colour.

They show how his ideas took shape: a stone-filled steel structure for the Digital Stones series, boats hung from a pole for Memory Motion, a lava project drawn as black blocks over red, and a monumental scheme for Documenta in Kassel. Together they follow his lifelong effort to set the pictorial tradition and changing technology side by side.

The show opens in mid December at the gallery's historic space near Piazza San Marco.

shows.title: I Give You My Heart, Venice
shows.description:
Lorenzo Quinn, the Italian-American sculptor best known for monumental hands, fills the gallery's historic space near Piazza San Marco with new bronzes and polished steel pieces gathered under the title I Give You My Heart. The show follows a winter presentation in Cortina d'Ampezzo and is renewed here with new works.

Hands and bodies reach, clasp and balance throughout: a golden heart held in cupped hands, two figures bending into a heart shape, a man leaning out of a mirrored bowl, and a tightrope walked by hands. The theme answers the Biennale's call for closer attention to small, human exchanges, and treats relationships between people as the way to imagine a future together.

The exhibition runs through the Biennale season and into early December.

shows.title: EMPORION: A Journey to the Center of the Earth in the Mediterranean
shows.description:
Andrea Valleri, a Venetian painter and sculptor who trained in philosophy, brings his Emporion project to Venice after its opening at the Archaeological Museum of Patras. The show is the second stage of a plan to connect Mediterranean hubs in search of a shared cultural identity, curated by Hara Hampsa and Marianna Savrami.

His work combines ancient Greek myth and landscape with a Pop Art language: bright paintings that pair images of the classical world with scrambled lettering, and tall figures built from wood and stone that echo Plato's idea of memory as recollection. Shown at the Museo Storico Navale, they sit among the Republic's maritime history.

The Venice presentation was organised through Galleria d'Arte Contini and runs to late November.

venue.name: Galleria d'Arte Contini
venue.address: Museo Storico Navale, Riva San Biagio, Castello 2148

shows.title: Andres Serrano: Sacro e Profano, 1983-2019
shows.description:
Andres Serrano's Venice survey, Sacro e profano, runs from his 1983 Crucifix to the Infamous portraits of 2019 and shows why a photographer who always works in the studio became one of the most argued-over image makers of his generation. The curator, Valerio Dehò, built it around the push and pull between the sacred and the profane.

The Immersion series is the heart of it, with sacred and artistic subjects photographed in glowing yellow-red fluid, where the liquid heightens the symbol's power instead of mocking it. Around it hang the Morgue pictures, such as Fatal Meningitis, the staged portraits of Nomads and Infamous, the 2011 Holy Works, and a 2004 portrait of Donald Trump from the America series.

Taboos of sexuality, the hooded figures of the Klan and anonymous dead people recur as other themes. Serrano has said his posed portraits are self-portraits, since his sitters arrive dressed and ready to become icons.

venue.name: Galleria Michela Rizzo
venue.address: Palazzo Palumbo Fossati Fondamenta della Malvasia Vecchia, Fondamenta Narisi, 2597, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: From Chaos to Freedom
shows.description:
François Reboul, a French painter who worked as a doctor before painting full time and now lives in Venice, shows large abstract canvases that take American Abstract Expressionism as a starting point. He paints straight onto the canvas with no preparatory drawing, letting gesture, paint and time decide the picture.

This is the second chapter of a two-part project. Where the first looked at chaos, this one follows the move from disorder toward balance and inner freedom. Two newly made diptychs anchor the show, one on each floor of the former Scoletta of San Zaccaria: a ground-floor composition of golden fields cut by cobalt blue, and an upstairs work of deep reds, blues and violets against black and ivory marks.

Smaller canvases of various formats surround them and show different ways the same tension between chaos and freedom can resolve.

venue.name: Galleria d'Arte San Vidal
venue.address: Campo S. Zaccaria, 4693, 30122 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Ferdinando Scianna al Ghetto di Venezia
shows.description:
Ferdinando Scianna, the Sicilian photographer who joined Magnum at Henri Cartier-Bresson's invitation, shows his black-and-white pictures of the Venetian Ghetto, made in 2016 for the five-hundredth anniversary of its founding. The pictures walk through the Campo del Ghetto Nuovo, over its three bridges and up its unusually tall buildings, and treat the place as a living neighbourhood rather than a monument.

The gallery sits in the same campo, so the show is hung a few steps from its subject. It was put together by gallery founder Ziva Kraus, who walked the Ghetto with Scianna during the shoot, and Federico Piccaluga.

Scianna's frontal, theatrical, light-and-shadow style gives the Ghetto's reflections, doorways and quiet corners the weight of a stage set.

venue.name: Ikona Gallery
venue.address: Campo del Ghetto Nuovo, Cannaregio 2909, 30121 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: L'Ambrosia purpurea
shows.description:
Greta Ferretti, born in Rome in 1996 and based in Venice, has her first solo show at Marignana Gallery's main space. Her paintings and mixed-media works on paper build an inner landscape of invented places, half-remembered people and loose destinies, a private mythology in which memory and imagination keep overlapping.

The title borrows ambrosia, the food that kept the gods immortal, and the show turns on permanence and change: figures and scenes surface, dissolve and come back rearranged. None of them points to a named identity; they read as presences with untold stories.

A text by Marta Varini accompanies the exhibition, which opens at the end of November.

shows.title: Materia e Codice
shows.description:
Matteo Mandelli's solo show at Marignana Project is about what happens when technology stops being a tool and starts acting like a counterpart. It gathers three bodies of work: the Cyber Carpets, where woven Persian-style patterns are crossed with electronic components and circuits; The Contact, a series of LCD screens engraved until they become unpredictable surfaces; and a piece from The Algorithm Creed.

That last series, which won him the first Berlendis Venice Art Prize, is the most personal. A confessional-like cabinet treats the algorithm as something you speak to, raising questions of trust, listening and authority.

The show sets physical material against digital mediation and asks how devices now shape perception, memory and ritual.

shows.title: I Ritratti Perduti / The Lost Portraits, 1990-2025
shows.description:
Maurizio Pellegrin looks back across thirty-five years of making to follow one thread, the portrait that has lost its face. Old photographs, a nineteenth-century canvas, a sixteenth-century panel and a 1919 drawing are painted over, blotted with colour, hung with cord or cloth, until the sitter is only a trace.

The works range from small cabinet-card portraits stamped with red to an oxide-on-wood series built on century-old drawings and a Christ head bound with black fabric. Rather than confirming who someone was, they scatter identity and leave it fragile.

Made mostly before selfie culture, the pieces keep a quiet, private tone, and the show reads as a long argument against the demand to be seen. It was organised with Galleria Michela Rizzo.

shows.title: Mario Testino
shows.description:
Mario Testino, the photographer long known for fashion and portrait work for Vogue, gives Venice a show that moves between his two sides. Large prints of models in Jaipur, New York and Los Angeles sit beside still lifes of Meissen porcelain ewers, and a pale horse photographed in Uzbekistan stands in near-darkness.

Five-panel floral works, shown as long friezes of dark and golden blooms, run along the gallery wall and link the Tokyo and London pictures to the Meissen series. The porcelain pictures are named for the four elements, Earth, Air and Fire among them, and are photographed against saturated backgrounds that treat the figurines like portrait sitters.

The exhibition is the gallery's autumn presentation in Venice and closes in mid November.

shows.title: Dress Rehearsal
shows.description:
Sara Berman's first solo show in Venice is a cast of harlequins, pierrots and clowns, all drawn from the same performer: the artist herself, photographed in costumes she makes. Oil paintings on linen, some in triptychs, sit beside dense pen-and-ink studies of the same figures.

Each painting starts from a harlequin pattern laid down first and then painted over until the figures emerge half-hidden, caught in poses of fear, grace, longing and loss. Titles such as Music Maker, Pierrot, The Fool, Ringmaster and Aviatrix name the characters, and a few pictures crop to a gloved hand on a belted hip or a bent leg.

The show treats the jester as a woman's trickster role, a way of resisting fixed identity and the way women are looked at. It opens in late November and runs into February.

shows.title: The Glass Aquarium
shows.artist: Dale Chihuly, Lino Tagliapietra, Maria Grazia Rosin, Tristano di Robilant, within Austin Young: Marriage of the Sea
shows.description:
The Glass Aquarium is a show of studio glass from four makers: Lino Tagliapietra and Dale Chihuly, the two giants who worked together and shaped each other's blowing, and the younger Maria Grazia Rosin and Tristano di Robilant. Chihuly's early Seaform sets appear alongside Tagliapietra's virtuoso Murano forms.

Rosin brings creatures of the deep into the home, hung or set on a table in opaline and mirrored glass; di Robilant works in silica forms about poetry and literature, drawn with master glassblower Zilio and then blown.

The glass is placed inside Austin Young's Marriage of the Sea (Il Ratto di Venezia), a photographic environment that covers the piano nobile of Palazzo Cesari Marchesi in images drawn from Venetian decorative tradition and allegorical painting. The exhibition is presented by The Pool NYC.

venue.name: The Pool NYC at Palazzo Cesari Marchesi
venue.address: San Marco, 30100 Venice, Metropolitan City of Venice, Italy

shows.title: TROPPA
shows.description:
Dora Fiammetta Perini, born in New York in 1995 and working between Venice and London, treats the body as source, container and compass. TROPPA, which means 'too much' in Italian, uses food as the lens for control, addiction, nourishment and vulnerability.

Sculpture, installation, photography and performance set off a kind of digestive process in which reality is chewed up and reduced to household waste. Pictures show a figure bent over a kitchen floor, a steel trolley loaded with pale forms, and painted and cast pieces set in the bare rooms of the gallery.

The show, curated by Luca Berta and Francesca Giubilei, asks whether waste can stop being a failure and become a chance for expression.

venue.name: Galleria d'Arte Santo Stefano
venue.address: Campo Santo Stefano, 2828a, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Epic Tales
shows.description:
Yang SoonYeal's first major solo show in Venice fills the State Rooms of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta with tall, rainbow-gradient figures shaped like gowned maternal bodies and dark, glossy, lumpy bronze-like forms that sit on the floor among the chandeliers and frescoes.

The Korean artist, who trained in Oriental painting and has made a career out of the figure of the mother, treats the instinct to care as an ethical answer to a fragmented world. The title, Epic Tales, points to myth and metamorphosis, with a Surrealist reading of the cosmic mother.

The show was organised by Baahng Projects as an independent parallel program to the 61st Biennale and curated by Jennifer Baahng.

venue.name: Galleria d'Arte Santo Stefano
venue.address: Campo Santo Stefano, 2828a, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Darkness Visible: The Long Shadow of Dictatorship
shows.artist: Nineteen Argentine and international artists and collectives; curated by Victoria Noorthoorn, Patricio Orellana and Augusto Maurandi
shows.description:
Darkness Visible marks fifty years since the 1976 coup that began Argentina's last military dictatorship, a regime of censorship, torture, kidnapping and the forced disappearance of some 30,000 people. It was devised by the Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires and installed at Spazio Punch on the Giudecca, with nineteen artists and collectives whose work runs from the 1970s to now.

The show is arranged as a walk through time. Visitors meet León Ferrari's newspaper pages and Marcelo Brodsky's photographs first, both artists who lost family to the disappearances. Further in are Luis Camnitzer's Execution, a shattered mirror that puts the viewer in the line of fire, Eduardo Gil's pictures of the 1983 Siluetazo, Gianni Mestichelli's censored mime photographs, Guillermo Kuitca's recent drawings of empty rooms and chairs, and Marta Minujin's toppled-monument projects.

The later rooms turn to the post-dictatorship underground: the performance group La Organización Negra, Liliana Maresca, Marcos López, Sergio De Loof and the Archivo de la Memoria Trans. The title borrows Milton's phrase for the light of Hell, a way of saying that art can make visible what was hidden or censored.

venue.name: Spazio Punch
venue.address: Fondamenta S. Biagio, 800/o, 30133 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: Celia Paul: Objects of Desire
shows.description:
Celia Paul shows new oil paintings made around Giorgione's La Tempesta, the Accademia picture she first became fixated on during a residency in the gallery's studio above the Giudecca Canal. The title work reworks the scene of a standing man and a seated, nursing woman, set apart by a strip of water.

The other canvases turn the same question on herself. Tramonto: Watching Painter borrows the composition of a Lucian Freud portrait of her, and Naked Painter and Seated Painter put the artist both behind and in front of the gaze. Throughout, the subject is looking and being looked at.

The show opens alongside her memoir Objects of Desire: An Artist in Venice, a record of obsession, loss and making in the city, and the paintings can be read as its visual counterpart.

venue.name: Victoria Miro Venice
venue.address: Calle Drio la Chiesa, 1994, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy

shows.title: In Minor Keys (Arsenale)
shows.artist: 54 artists and collectives, conceived by Koyo Kouoh
shows.description:
The Arsenale half of the 61st Biennale Arte main exhibition, In Minor Keys, was conceived by the late curator Koyo Kouoh. It gathers 54 artists and collectives whose work moves between sound, film, sculpture, textile, archive and ritual, and it treats the minor key as a way of listening to quieter, overlooked histories.

Across the long brick halls, Laurie Anderson's charcoal drawing environment, Nick Cave's armored figures, Kader Attia's reflections on repair, Berni Searle's chapel projection and Carsten Hoeller's mushroom forms sit near the archives of Pauline Oliveros and Gala Porras-Kim. Many pieces are collaborative or rooted in communities, from Blaxtarlines Kumasi's school to Guadalupe Maravilla's healing sculptures.

One artist, Fabrice Aragno, shows separately at Forte Marghera. The exhibition stays open to November 22, 2026, and it is the most direct view of Kouoh's final curatorial vision.

shows.title: In Minor Keys (Central Pavilion)
shows.artist: 55 artists, curated by the late Koyo Kouoh
shows.description:
In Minor Keys is the main exhibition of the 61st Venice Biennale, conceived by the late Koyo Kouoh and carried out by her team. Its Central Pavilion section at the Giardini gathers 55 artists and collectives, many of them from Africa and its diasporas, the Caribbean, South Asia and the Pacific.

The title borrows from music: a minor key is quieter and more tender than a major one. The works favour intimacy, memory and repair over spectacle, with ink drawings of looted objects, smoke-fired ceramics, embroidery, photography, film, sculpture and installation sitting alongside a work by Marcel Duchamp.

Many of the artists are shown in the Central Pavilion and also in the Arsenale, so the exhibition reads as one conversation across both venues. It runs until 22 November 2026.

shows.title: Leiko Ikemura: La forma della luce
shows.description:
Leiko Ikemura's glass sculptures are placed among the paintings of the Gallerie dell'Accademia, so her small, pale figures face Venetian masters. Cast in translucent glass, hares, busts and winged creatures glow amber, lilac or clear.

The show is part of the tenth Venice Glass Week and was curated by Isabella Collavizza. It treats glass as a way of holding light, and links the artist's long interest in figures between human and animal with the Venetian tradition of colour.

shows.title: Patrick Saytour: Le pli et le temps / La piega e il tempo
shows.description:
The first exhibition in Italy of Patrick Saytour, a French artist associated with the Supports/Surfaces group, fills the rooms of Palazzo Vendramin Grimani. Folded, dyed and stitched cloth, paper and tile-like forms show his way of making a work out of folds and repeated marks.

The show was curated by Daniela Ferretti and sets the soft, worn materials against the palazzo's old frescoes and gilding, tying the idea of time to the fold.

venue.name: Fondazione dell'Albero d'Oro – Palazzo Vendramin Grimani

shows.title: Ceal Floyer: Unfinished
shows.description:
A posthumous show of Ceal Floyer, who died in December 2025, takes its title from Unfinished (1995), a looped film of two thumbs twiddling that is projected on the corner of a low wall or step. Curated by Ann Gallagher and Jonathan Watkins, it gathers the dry, precise works she made from ordinary things such as buckets, a mousehole and printed numbers.

Floyer turned small jokes and plain facts into pieces about perception and language. In the rooms of Palazzo Diedo they sit lightly and do not announce themselves.

shows.title: Penumbra
shows.description:
Penumbra turns a one-night performance into a lasting installation. On 7 May the musician Kelsey Lu staged a live piece in Palazzo Diedo, and what it left behind, soil, sound and charcoal, was reworked with the photographer Yumna Al-Arashi into a room-scale work that opened on 8 July.

The piece is organised around three realms, earth, dream and collapse, and draws on Lu's album So Help Me God and on Al-Arashi's photographs of land, memory and survival. It sits against the frescoed rooms of the palazzo and runs alongside Strange Rules and the Ceal Floyer show.

shows.title: Strange Rules
shows.artist: Group show (30+ artists incl. Trevor Paglen, Hito Steyerl, Philippe Parreno, Lynn Hershman Leeson)
shows.description:
Strange Rules is a large group show on Protocol Art, work that treats code, algorithms, AI models and biological systems as an artist's material. It was conceived by Mat Dryhurst, Holly Herndon and Hans Ulrich Obrist with Adriana Rispoli, and gathers more than thirty artists in the rooms of Palazzo Diedo.

The pieces range from video and sculpture to systems that keep changing, and ask who sets the rules behind the images and sounds we meet every day.

shows.title: Metamorphosis: Beyond the Real. Searching for Victoria Lu
shows.description:
A retrospective and open research project on Victoria Lu, built around more than fifty years of work. Archive material, AI-generated pieces and moving-image projects are arranged in four sections called Generation, Translation, Recomposition and Co-Writing.

The show asks whether curating can change when humans and AI think together, and is part of the China and the Arts programme tied to the Biennale. The curators are Angelo Maggi, Fei Jun, Sen Fu and Chuang Cheng-chi.

shows.title: Jenny Saville a Ca' Pesaro
shows.description:
Ca' Pesaro gives Jenny Saville her first large show in Venice: around thirty monumental paintings from the early 1990s to now. Her subject is the body, painted in thick, fleshy strokes that borrow from old master painting and from medical imagery.

The last room holds new works made in response to Venice, set among the museum's own modern collection. The exhibition was curated by Elisabetta Barisoni with support from Gagosian.

shows.title: Nel segno di Venezia: the Favaretto Rubelli donation
shows.artist: Palma il Giovane, Sebastiano Ricci, Gaspare Diziani, Francesco Fontebasso, Giambattista Tiepolo and others
shows.description:
Alessandro Favaretto Rubelli, whose family runs the Rubelli textile house, has given 29 drawings and prints to the city's museum foundation, and Ca' Rezzonico shows them together for the first time. They range from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century, running from Palma il Giovane to Tiepolo.

The sheets are hung on a grey wall in the museum's rooms, framed in the old gilt and wood frames of a collector's house. They include a preparatory drawing by Sebastiano Ricci for his Temptations of Saint Anthony, two studies by his pupil Gaspare Diziani, and a youthful copy by Francesco Fontebasso after his master. Alberto Craievich curated it, and it adds to the museum's growing cabinet of drawings of the Venetian eighteenth century.

shows.title: Glasstress 2026
shows.artist: Group show, more than 50 artists (Ventura, Le Bas, Wurm, Prouvost, Cardillo, Wang and others)
shows.description:
Glasstress, the Berengo Foundation's long-running experiment, returns with more than fifty artists who each made work in glass with the master glassmakers of Berengo Studio. About twenty of them are new to the project and many are touching glass for the first time, so the results run from playful to strange.

The Venice half in Palazzo Ca' Tron on the Grand Canal includes a spiky blue dog by Ronald Ventura, a glass house with grasping red hands by Delaine Le Bas, a yellow egg on green legs by Erwin Wurm, a pink-and-blue creature with a plug for a tail by Laure Prouvost, a dressed pair of figures by Ornella Cardillo and a stacked totem by Ziping Wang. A second part is at the Berengo Art Space on Murano. Adriano Berengo, Joanna De Vos and Umberto Croppi curated it.

shows.title: Bizhan Bassiri: Principe. Il Nottambulo del Pensiero Magmatico
shows.description:
Bizhan Bassiri takes over a room of the Museo Correr, the Sala delle Quattro Porte in the picture gallery designed by Carlo Scarpa, and turns it into a gallery of his own. Recent works and pieces tied to his long research hang in rows beneath a chandelier.

The central figure is the Principe, a night-walking alter ego who stands for what the artist calls magmatic thought. The show was curated by Chiara Squarcina and Bruno Corà.

shows.title: Spiral Economy: Charrière and Canova
shows.description:
Part of the Correr's Dialoghi Canoviani series, this show puts the work of Julian Charrière in conversation with Antonio Canova's neoclassical sculpture. Charrière's films and objects follow materials such as ash, ice and minerals through cycles of making and decay.

Canova's marble figures stand for an ideal of lasting beauty, and the pairing sets that against a present in which extraction and waste shape how things last.

shows.title: Personal Structures: Confluences
shows.artist: Group show of international artists (Palazzo Bembo, Palazzo Mora, Marinaressa Gardens)
shows.description:
The eighth Personal Structures exhibition spreads artists from many countries through Palazzo Bembo, Palazzo Mora and the Marinaressa Gardens. The theme, Confluences, speaks to a world of fractures, displacement and fast change, and the artists respond with painting, sculpture, installation and video.

Among the highlights is a Heinz Mack retrospective, Color in Forma, at Palazzo Bembo. The show alternates each year with Time Space Existence and is free to enter.

venue.name: European Cultural Centre (Palazzo Mora / Palazzo Bembo)
venue.address: Palazzo Bembo, Riva del Carbon 4793; Palazzo Mora, Strada Nova 3659, Venice

shows.title: Lydia Ourahmane: 5 Works
shows.description:
Lydia Ourahmane fills the Nicoletta Fiorucci Foundation's Dorsoduro palazzo with five works, most of them built from humble materials and everyday routines. A beaded curtain, a pot of soup simmering on a gas ring, a coin dropped into a metal box and stacks of crumpled white cloth sit in rooms with terrazzo floors and bare plaster.

The show grew out of a residency at the foundation and draws on Venice's position as a port between Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa. A pier designed to be moved to the island of Poveglia, wall-mounted contact sheets and a plaster cast of a carved head give the rooms a sense of passage and loss. Polly Staple curated it, and it runs through 22 November.

shows.title: Helter Skelter: Arthur Jafa and Richard Prince
shows.description:
Two American artists who both build their work out of other people's images share the two floors and courtyard of Ca' Corner della Regina. Curated by Nancy Spector, the show gathers more than fifty photographs, videos, sculptures, paintings and installations, some never shown before, and a zine the two made together.

Jafa cuts film, news footage, music video and social media into tense, rhythmic videos and objects about Black life. Prince re-photographs pulp, advertising, motorcycle culture and jokes, and turns them into a portrait of masculinity and myth. Hung side by side, the pair read as a rough anthology of American violence, desire and style, which is why many reviewers called it the real American pavilion of the Biennale.

venue.name: Fondazione Prada
venue.address: Calle de Ca' Corner, Santa Croce 2215, 30135 Venice

shows.title: Erwin Wurm: Dreamers
shows.description:
Erwin Wurm's first big solo show in Italy sets his sculptures among the clutter of the Fortuny palazzo. New pieces appear for the first time alongside works from several of his best-known series, where clothes, furniture and everyday objects stand in for bodies.

Garments slump, bend and stand upright on their own, and the figures seem to sleep, dream or hide. Placed against the old portraits and fabrics of the house, the humour and unease of the sculptures take on a second layer.

shows.title: Bertil Vallien: Transparent Boundaries / Martin Janecký: Dreamers
shows.description:
Palazzo Franchetti pairs two solo shows by glass sculptors from different generations. Bertil Vallien, born in 1938, shows his sand-cast glass boats, long vessels packed with small images and objects that stand for journeys, memory and the passage of a life, alongside heads cast in glass.

Martin Janecký, born in 1980, works the opposite way. He shapes molten glass from the inside of the bubble, a rare technique that lets him make close-to-life heads, masks and sleeping or huddled figures with striking realism. Jean Blanchaert curated the pairing for Berengo Studio, setting transparency against solidity and symbolism against exact observation.

shows.title: Amoako Boafo: It doesn't have to always make sense
shows.description:
Amoako Boafo's first solo show in Italy fills the upper floor of the Museo di Palazzo Grimani with new portraits made for its rooms. His Ghanaian and Black diasporic sitters are painted in thick, finger-smeared strokes, often in flat cut-out shapes of white clothing set against dark or saturated grounds.

Hung in a palazzo whose lower floor holds the Grimani family's Renaissance portraits, the paintings enter a conversation with Venetian portrait tradition. The works range from a sitter in a lace-patterned top on a deep red ground to a woman reclining on a flowered sofa, and from a parent holding a child to pairs of women in bright dresses. Gagosian produced the exhibition, which closes on 22 November.

shows.title: Fucina degli Angeli: Peggy Guggenheim and 20th-Century Artistic Glass
shows.artist: Jean Cocteau, Max Ernst, Hans Arp and others
shows.description:
This show tells the story of the Fucina degli Angeli, the Murano glass workshop founded by Egidio Costantini, where twentieth-century artists made their designs into glass. More than one hundred glass works, drawings and documents show how Picasso, Cocteau, Ernst, Arp and others worked with the furnace masters.

Peggy Guggenheim supported the Fucina at key moments, and the show sets the glass beside paintings and sculptures from her own collection. Curated by Cristina Beltrami, it travels on to London and New York.

venue.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
venue.address: Palazzo Venier dei Leoni, Dorsoduro 701, 30123 Venice

shows.title: We Rise by Lifting Others
shows.description:
Marinella Senatore made this piece for the Human Safety Net's space above Piazza San Marco after workshops with families in Warsaw, Mestre and Palermo, using writing, storytelling and movement. The phrases that came out of those sessions are stitched and lit into the finished work.

A light sculpture about four metres high, her first in a new luminaria style, rises like a Baroque candelabrum or the festive light towers of southern Italian saints' days. Around it hang six embroidered tapestries with stylised figures and words from the workshops, made in India at a craft school in Mumbai. The show sits beside the permanent exhibition A World of Potential and is free to enter.

venue.name: The Home of The Human Safety Net

shows.title: CHIHULY: Venice 2026
shows.description:
Dale Chihuly returns to Venice with three monumental glass towers set on the Grand Canal and an archive show inside Palazzo Loredan. The Gold Tower rises in a palazzo garden, a Blue and Green Tower stands in another courtyard, and an End of the Day Chandelier crowns a rooftop terrace, all visible from the water.

Inside the Istituto Veneto, a darkened room holds Celadon Baskets and other smaller blown forms, with a long light table of photographs and faxes recalling Chihuly Over Venice, the 1990s project in which glassblowers worked in Venetian and Finnish workshops. Suzanne Geiss curated the archive exhibition, which closes on 14 November.

venue.name: Istituto Veneto (Palazzo Loredan)
venue.address: Campo Santo Stefano, San Marco 2945, 30124 Venice

shows.title: Sanya Kantarovsky: Basic Failure
shows.description:
Sanya Kantarovsky's Venice show hangs new paintings, ceramics and a glass head made with a Murano studio inside the sixteenth-century Palazzo Loredan, home of the Istituto Veneto. His figures are pale, hunched or tumbling: a boy with a cigarette, a swimmer face down in water, a black horse falling over a collapsed body.

The pictures play off the library-like rooms and the Narcissus story, with mirrors, reflection and failure as running themes. Critics have called the show bleak but striking. It stays open until 22 November.

venue.name: Istituto Veneto (Palazzo Loredan)
venue.address: Campo Santo Stefano, San Marco 2945, 30124 Venice

shows.title: 1948-1958 Il vetro di Murano e la Biennale di Venezia
shows.description:
This third chapter of Le Stanze del Vetro's study of Murano glass at the Biennale covers the decade of postwar rebirth, with more than 160 pieces. It follows how the island's glassmakers moved from tradition to modern design, in works shown at the Biennale pavilions between 1948 and 1958.

The show, curated by Marino Barovier, pairs the glass with period photographs and documents of the Biennale, and shows how architects and artists such as Carlo Scarpa worked with the furnaces.

venue.name: Le Stanze del Vetro
venue.address: Isola di San Giorgio Maggiore, 30133 Venice

shows.title: Alfred Eisenstaedt: La fotografia era nell'aria
shows.description:
The Museo Storico Navale, beside the Arsenale, shows the Venice half of a two-venue retrospective on Alfred Eisenstaedt, the Life photographer who made some of the twentieth century's best-known pictures. This part concentrates on his years in Europe between the wars and on the portraits and magazine stories that followed.

The selection runs from the sailor kissing a nurse on V-J Day to Sophia Loren laughing at a table, Walt Disney's brother among a wall of toys, a roadside Michelin advertisement and a crowd of children gasping at a puppet show. Monica Poggi curated the show for CAMERA in Turin; the companion section at Villa Bassi Rathgeb in Abano Terme closed in September.

venue.name: Museo Storico Navale
venue.address: Campo San Biagio, Riva San Biagio, Castello 2148, 30122 Venice

shows.title: Luca Bertolo: L'inizio ci assale
shows.description:
Palazzetto Marcello, a new exhibition space near Santa Maria Formosa, opens with Luca Bertolo. Some forty works, many shown for the first time, are spread over two floors under a single theme: the beginning of a painting, of a life, of a culture, and how it is tangled up with the end.

The rooms mix portraits in old frames, canvases hung loose from a wall, small coloured-pencil drawings after Leonardo, Dürer and Van Gogh, and a new series of tall wooden staffs fitted with bones, feathers and brushes, which recall tribal totems. The title comes from a line by the poet Milo De Angelis. Elena Volpato curated the show, which runs until 14 February 2027.

shows.title: Heinz Mack: Color in Forma
shows.description:
A birthday retrospective for Heinz Mack, who turned 95 in 2026 and co-founded the ZERO group in 1957. The show gathers around three dozen paintings from the last decade, most of them never shown before, in which pure colour is set out in grids, stacked blocks and nested squares.

The pictures look back to the ZERO interest in light and vibration but are built entirely from colour. Chequered fields of small coloured squares sit beside tall towers of saturated blue, red and yellow, so a visitor can follow how one simple idea keeps changing. His son-in-law Marc Mack curated the exhibition, which closes on 22 November.

venue.name: European Cultural Centre (Palazzo Mora / Palazzo Bembo)

shows.title: Amar Kanwar: Co-Travellers
shows.description:
Amar Kanwar closes the Palazzo Grassi season with two multi-channel film installations on the upper floor. The Peacock's Graveyard, from 2023, spreads seven screens through a dark room, while The Torn First Pages, made between 2004 and 2008, follows the long struggle for democracy in Myanmar.

Kanwar works slowly, combining images of nature, objects and testimony. The films treat landscape, memory and political violence together, and ask the viewer to move between screens rather than follow a single story.

venue.name: Palazzo Grassi
venue.address: Campo San Samuele, San Marco 3231, 30124 Venice

shows.title: Michael Armitage: The Promise of Change
shows.description:
The largest survey yet of Michael Armitage fills Palazzo Grassi with around forty-five paintings and a large body of preparatory studies. Made in Nairobi on lubugo bark cloth, the pictures draw on Kenyan politics, migration, violence and myth, and on a long line of European painting that the artist reworks from an East African point of view.

The title comes from a 2018 canvas and holds hope and doubt together. The paintings do not offer a verdict or a solution; they give room to sit with uneasy feelings. Amar Kanwar's film installations share the building and close the show on the upper floor.

venue.name: Palazzo Grassi
venue.address: Campo San Samuele, San Marco 3231, 30124 Venice

shows.title: Lorna Simpson: Third Person
shows.description:
Lorna Simpson's first large European survey in over a decade shows more than ten years of painting, organized with the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Deep blue and black canvases, built from ink, silkscreen and washes, hang in the long brick halls of the Dogana.

The paintings sit with her glacier-ice sculptures and stacks of old magazines, which keep the focus on memory, race and the way images of Black women circulate. The curator is Emma Lavigne.

shows.title: Paulo Nazareth: Algebra
shows.description:
Paulo Nazareth, who walks long distances as part of his art, fills the second hall of Punta della Dogana with objects, drawings and films gathered on his journeys through the Americas and Africa. Worn sandals, handwritten pages and portraits of people he met sit on pallets and walls.

The title points to his habit of balancing unlike things against each other: migration, race, labour and the way a body carries a place. The show is curated by Fernanda Brenner.

shows.title: Cosmotechnics: Ding Yi as a Planetary Code
shows.description:
Ding Yi, the Shanghai painter known for grids of small crosses, has his first Venice show in the rooms of the Querini Stampalia. It follows more than four decades of abstract work, from older pieces to new panels made for the palazzo.

The centre of the show is the Appearance of Crosses series: tall acrylic and woodcut panels on linden wood, each repeating a simple mark until it reads as pattern, light and system. The curators frame the crosses as a kind of code, a way of thinking about technology and the planet through a single repeated sign.

shows.title: Nigel Cooke: Bad Habits
shows.description:
Nigel Cooke's first solo show in Italy grew out of a residency at the Querini Stampalia, where he was given the library's long Portego as a working studio. The new paintings were made there over months, in the middle of the foundation's old books and furniture.

The canvases are large, dark and dense, built from tangled fragments of figures and ruin, with small areas of light that the artist likens to moonlit pieces of hope. Pace Gallery followed the Venice paintings with a related show of smaller works.

shows.title: The Quiet Source
shows.description:
Jan Fabre is the first living artist invited to place work inside the Scuola Grande di San Rocco, the confraternity hall whose walls and ceilings are covered by Tintoretto's great painting cycle. He shows three new silicon bronze sculptures, laid out along the building's central axis between the lower and upper floors.

The figures include a standing man holding a sword, titled Oath of My Father, and The Man Who Cuts the Grass, set in the Sala dell'Albergo under Tintoretto's glory of Saint Roch. A third piece, The Artist as a Stray Dog in His Basket, sits in the upper rooms. The bronzes took about five years to make and are meant to be read against Tintoretto's scenes of mercy and protection, the purpose the Scuola was founded for.

venue.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
venue.address: San Polo 3052, Campo San Rocco, 30125 Venice

shows.title: Alighiero Boetti
shows.description:
SMAC Venice, the restored Procuratie on Piazza San Marco, gives Alighiero Boetti a survey of about a hundred works in eight rooms, covering the late 1960s to the early 1990s. It opens with self-portraits and the idea of the double, from the moment in 1972 when he started signing as Alighiero e Boetti.

From there the show follows his systems of language, geography and time: embroidered world maps, grids of letters hidden in coloured embroidery, the Aerei series of flying machines, the Calendari and the rigorous series of works on paper from the 1980s and early 1990s. Elena Geuna curated it with the Archivio Alighiero Boetti and Ben Brown Fine Arts, and it closes on 22 November.

shows.title: Joseph Kosuth: The exchange value of language has fallen to zero
shows.description:
Joseph Kosuth, a founder of conceptual art, fills the Berggruen Institute's Casa dei Tre Oci on the Giudecca with work about how language makes meaning. A new large-scale piece, A Chain of Resemblance (2026), greets visitors at the entrance, and a wall neon, One and Eight, spells out a sentence in light across a plastered palazzo room.

Upstairs the show goes back to the early 1960s with a grid of framed photographs and text works, setting his first experiments next to the latest. The title points at a language worn thin by constant media circulation. Mario Codognato and Adriana Rispoli curated it, and it runs through 22 November.

shows.title: Penelope: Her Journeys
shows.artist: Gayle Chong Kwan, Stephanie Blake, Kimiko Yoshida
shows.description:
The second part of a trilogy drawn from Homer's Odyssey, this show looks at Penelope, the one who waits at home, and treats her waiting as a journey of its own. Three artists, Gayle Chong Kwan, Stephanie Blake and Kimiko Yoshida, respond with photography, installation and image-making.

It follows Telemachus, shown here in 2025, and was curated by Francesca Giubilei and Valentina Secco at Palazzo Bonvicini.

shows.title: An Iconography of American Beauty
shows.description:
Mel Ramos (1935 to 2018) was a California Pop painter who turned pin-up girls into glossy modern Venuses. This show gathers his paintings of nudes posed on candy wrappers and chocolate boxes, comic-book heroines and the classical reclining nude, all painted with the smooth finish of a magazine advertisement.

Unlike Warhol or Lichtenstein, who borrowed the look of advertising, Ramos set its imagery beside the old art-historical models of female beauty. The exhibition shows how desire is both celebrated and manufactured in these pictures, and centres on his wife Leta, who was his long-time muse. Admission is free in the palazzo near San Zaccaria.

shows.title: A Place in the Sun
shows.description:
Genti Korini's three-channel film installation imagines a theatre staged entirely in Zaum, the made-up, grammar-free language of Russian avant-garde poets. Actors, puppets with painted ceramic-like faces, computer-built landscapes, masked mountain figures and a stately woman in black pass across a wide band of screens in a dark room, with an original score underneath.

The project starts from a 1916 issue of an avant-garde magazine published in Petersburg that mocked exotic European fantasies about Albania, and from a puppet play about Yanko, the King of Albania. Korini uses that odd source to ask how a place is invented by outsiders and by itself, and to honour minor languages and invisible cultures.

Curated by Malgorzata Ludwisiak, it links the unease of today to a century-old moment when borders, languages and identities were unsettled. Korini's geometric coloured drawings and a painting accompany the film.

shows.title: MONITOR YIN YANG
shows.description:
Matías Duville fills the Argentine pavilion with a walkable drawing made of salt and charcoal, spread across the floor like a white terrain etched with black marks. Hills of salt carry drawn forests, a vacuum cleaner, a car, a ringed planet and a ribbed hull, so the whole room reads as a landscape that was once lived in and has since been left to the elements.

A dark control room off the main space holds a bank of screens and a seated figure, which turns the terrain into something watched. Sound and video run through the installation, and visitors' movements activate it, so the surveilled ground changes as people cross it.

The project sets the end of a feared future against the stubborn human habit of finding beauty in disaster. Salt and charcoal, residues of seas and forests, stand for geological and human time at once, making this Duville's largest drawing to date.

shows.title: The Studio
shows.description:
Zadik Zadikian turns the Armenian pavilion into a working studio. Throughout the exhibition he and assistants cast, pigment and stack plaster bricks of different sizes, so the objects on view keep growing and rearranging as visitors watch.

The results are bright blocks and slabs in red, pink, turquoise, yellow and green that sit in a big Arsenale hall like a colour-field landscape. Process, labour and play are as much on show as the finished sculpture.

It was first announced under another title, Ode to Lord Byron, and was curated by Tony Shafrazi and Tina Chakarian.

venue.name: Armenia Pavilion
venue.address: Fondamenta Case Nuove 2738/C, Castello, Tesa 41, Arsenale Militare

shows.title: conference of one's self
shows.description:
Khaled Sabsabi turns the Australia Pavilion into a walk-in painting of light and sound. Inside, moving images and a slow, pulsing soundtrack wrap the visitor, with shifting blue and violet brushwork that never settles into a single picture, so the line between the physical and the metaphysical keeps blurring. A wall of Arabic calligraphic marks adds a quieter layer.

The project draws on a twelfth-century Sufi poem about birds searching for their true king, and follows seven stages of doubt, love, knowledge, loss, learning and unlearning, before opening onto an eighth stage where change for a shared humanity becomes possible. Sabsabi, born in Lebanon and based in western Sydney since 1976, grounds it in migration and in multi-faith community life.

It matters as much for its history as for the work: his selection was withdrawn and then reinstated after a controversy in 2025, so the pavilion arrives as a statement about who gets to speak for a nation.

shows.title: Seaworld Venice
shows.description:
Florentina Holzinger turns the Austrian Pavilion into a working machine that runs on water and on the bodies of its performers. Inside, the hall is flooded and crossed by a tall column of dancers; a wave crashes through one room while a raft rides rushing water; mud, tanks and a bronze bell give the place the look of a theme park, a treatment plant and a chapel at once. Outside, portable toilets and a glass tank stand in the forecourt, and a crane sets performers working above the building and over the lagoon.

The piece treats water as something we drink, flush, fight over and drown in, and it makes visitors part of the cycle by feeding their own waste into the environments the performers live in. Holzinger, known for large-scale dance and theatre work, uses it to look at purity and pollution, guilt and cleansing, and the rubbish that cities push out of sight.

Curated by Nora-Swantje Almes, the pavilion is a live installation with scheduled performances, plus separate Etudes staged around Venice and its lagoon.

shows.title: The Attention
shows.description:
Faig Ahmed is known for taking the traditional Azerbaijani carpet and bending its pattern until it melts, pixelates or flows like liquid. For The Attention he extends that practice through several rooms of a Castello building, laying carpets underfoot and out through the doorway and hanging draped velvet like heavy water.

New pieces mix the textile craft with light, sound and electronics: a glowing disc against a wall of line drawings, a tall banner of paper falling from the ceiling, a standing screen of shifting text and a glass case full of wires and circuits. The point is the slow, focused kind of looking that weaving demands, set against the scattered attention of screens.

The pavilion is a solo presentation and one of the more physical in the Biennale's minor keys programme, where craft knowledge becomes the material for contemporary art.

shows.title: In Another Man's Yard
shows.description:
Two Bahamian artists share a Dorsoduro gallery and trade stories about home, labour and inherited history. Rooms painted deep blue, red and lilac hold carved and cut-out wooden figures that carry chains and machetes, a wall-sized painted panorama, wire and tin sculptures including a tall metal figure on a bicycle, and costumed Junkanoo-style figures in a darkened space.

The title points to the Bahamas' history of work done on someone else's land, from plantation labour to tourism today, and the way people still make their own culture inside it. Hanging blades, carved heads and drawn portraits turn tools of cutting and clearing into memorial forms.

The pairing is of two different hands, one working in hard fabricated metal and wood, the other in painting, collage and theatrical figures, but with a shared interest in carnival and ancestry.

shows.title: IT NEVER SSST
shows.description:
Miet Warlop turns the Belgian pavilion into an exhibition and a performance at once.
